key_insight: AD-DFPT can compute meta-GGA density-functional response derivatives by using algorithmic differentiation to avoid manual second-derivative XC formulas.
engineering_relevance: This makes advanced DFT response calculations and gradient-based functional training more practical for materials modeling workflows.
method: Recast XC second derivatives as Jacobian-vector products of the XC potentials.
Use algorithmic differentiation within an AD-DFPT framework.
Apply the approach to meta-GGA functionals such as r2SCAN01 and to neural-network XC optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports response-property calculations for ZnO and BaTiO3 and an optimization task on bulk silicon, with r2SCAN01 generally outperforming LDA and PBE.
watch_item: Accuracy and robustness depend on correct AD implementation and self-consistent convergence for meta-GGA XC terms, which can be more complex than standard GGA cases.
paper_title: Density functional perturbation theory of meta-generalized gradient approximations using algorithmic differentiation
